comment: D2 Round 24 — device verification strand vectors. Spec authority: crypto-media/device-verification.md. Three verification primitives: (a) cross-signing chain rooted at master key — each user has ONE master signing key (long-lived) that signs sub-keys for self-signing (per-device leaf sign) and user-signing (cross-user trust). (b) SAS (Short Authentication String) — Diffie-Hellman key exchange produces a short shared secret two parties compare to verify identity out-of-band. (c) Out-of-band emoji code — the SAS shared bytes map to an ordered list of emojis the two parties read/compare in person or over a trusted channel. The chain MUST validate at every link; SAS MUST agree on both sides; emoji codes MUST be deterministic from the shared secret bytes.

encoder.sas_algorithm: ECDH-X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 (8 bytes per emoji slot)

vectors.name: cross_signing_chain_master_signs_self_signing_signs_device_leaf
vectors.comment: Canonical chain: master_key → self_signing_key → device_leaf. The master key signs the self-signing key; the self-signing key signs the device leaf key. Both signatures verify.

expected.rationale: Chain valid: master signs self-signing; self-signing signs device leaf. Both signatures verify.

vectors.name: user_signing_cross_user_trust_link
vectors.comment: Cross-user trust: alice's user-signing key signs bob's master key, attesting that alice trusts bob's identity. The receiving relying party verifies (alice.user-signing → bob.master) link in addition to bob's own master→self chain.

expected.rationale: Cross-user trust: alice.user-signing signs bob.master, establishing alice→bob trust. Both signatures verify.

vectors.name: sas_verification_short_auth_string_match
vectors.comment: SAS verification: alice and bob each generate ECDH X25519 keypairs; exchange public keys; derive shared secret via HKDF-SHA256; truncate to a 6-byte short auth string both display. If the two parties compare the SAS out-of-band and match → verified.

expected.rationale: Both parties derive the same shared secret; the truncated SAS strings match → identity verified out-of-band.

vectors.name: out_of_band_emoji_code_deterministic_mapping
vectors.comment: The 6-byte SAS is also rendered as an ordered list of 7 emojis from the 64-symbol alphabet (each emoji = 6 bits, 7 emojis = 42 bits ≈ 6 bytes shown). The mapping is deterministic — the same shared bytes always map to the same emoji sequence on both sides.

expected.rationale: Emoji mapping is deterministic from shared bytes; both parties render identical sequence; OOB visual compare → verified.

vectors.name: self_signing_key_with_revoked_master_rejects
vectors.comment: Negative-shape variant: the master key has been revoked (e.g. user lost it and rotated to a new master). Any chain rooted at the OLD master MUST reject; clients must follow the new master's chain.

expected.rationale: Master key was revoked; any signature chain rooted at it MUST reject. Client must follow new master.
